title: Designing AI-Intensive Applications - swyx
talk_summary: This is swyx's opening keynote for the AI Engineer conference, mostly framing/state-of-the-field material: he proposes candidate 'standard models' for AI engineering (LLM OS, LLM SDLC, building-effective-agents, and his own SPAD loop) and argues the field should focus on human-input-to-AI-output ratio rather than agent-vs-workflow terminology. The only concrete mechanism is his description of AI News as a fixed scrape→plan→recursive-summarize→format→evaluate pipeline run daily, which he generalizes as SPAD.

takeaways.technique: Fixed SPAD pipeline instead of open-ended agent
takeaways.what_they_do: AI News is a deterministic pipeline: scrape sources, plan, recursively summarize in parallel, format, then evaluate — the same script repeated per source (Discord, Reddit, Twitter) rather than a free-form agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You scrape it. You plan. You recursively summarize. You format and you evaluate.

takeaways.technique: Input-to-output ratio as the design metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of arguing agent vs workflow, track the ratio of human input to valuable AI output per interaction and design to increase AI output per unit of human input, up to fully ambient (zero-input) agents.
Cites Anthropic/DeepMind/AMP examples where simple scaffolds beat elaborate ones on benchmarks; argues there is still 'alpha' in simplicity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the consistent lesson that we hear is to not over complicate things
